simple.meaning: אֲגָגִי (ʼĂgâgîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אֲגָגִי (H91) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Esther 3:1, with occurrences in Esther.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲגָגִי (H91) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אֲגָגִי (H91) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אֲגָגִי (ʼĂgâgîy) / H91 is traced through Esther 3:1, Esther 3:10, Esther 8:3, Esther 8:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

structuredEvidence.definition: an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag

firstOccurrence.englishText: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.

timeline.evidenceText: After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.
The king took his ring from his hand, and gave it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.
Esther spoke yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet, and begged him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his plan that he had planned against the Jews.

She said, “If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his sight, and the thing seem right to the king, and I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews who are in all the king’s provinces.
because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast “Pur”, that is the lot, to consume them, and to destroy them;

definitions.short: an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag
definitions.full: H91. Agagi אֲגָגִי adjective, of a people of Haman (= Amalekite ? so Jewish tradition & compare Jos Ant.xi.6 .5) Est 3:1 , 10 ; 8:3 , 5 ; 9:24 . אגד ( bind , so Talmud אָגַד , Aramaic אֲגַד ). **Aramaic ׳א (Talmud, once, Levy) probably Hebraism.
